source.author: Al Brooks
source.chapter_title: Globex, Premarket, Postmarket, and Overnight Market

conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode

candidates.name: PremarketExtremeTestTarget
candidates.quote: The premarket extremes are often targets that get tested during the day session.
candidates.description: The high/low made during the overnight/premarket session is often tested again once the day session opens; carry that level forward as a magnet/target that favors day-session entries trading toward it.
candidates.pseudocode:
premarketHigh = highest(high, sessionBars) // computed only over bars where ctx.Time() is within the premarket window, then held constant through the day session
close[0] <= premarketHigh + toleranceTicks * tickSize && close[0] >= premarketHigh - toleranceTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (a target/context level, not itself a specific order)

complexity.reason: requires segmenting bars into a premarket session by time-of-day, taking a highest/lowest over just that window, and holding the resulting level as a persistent target through the day session

notes: Brooks notes the premarket itself has few entries in the hour or two before the 6:30 a.m. PST open; this candidate is about using its extreme as a day-session target, not about trading the premarket directly.

candidates.name: CountertrendRequiresPriorTrendLineBreak
candidates.quote: Fade a strong trend only if there was first a trend line break.
candidates.description: Only take a countertrend (fade) entry against a strong trend if a trend line has already broken beforehand; blocks countertrend entries with no preceding trend-line break.
notes: trendLineBrokenRecently is the trend-line-break primitive defined in earlier chapters (e.g. V13-02's dependency); not redefined here.

candidates.name: CountertrendSignalBarMinimumTimeframe
candidates.quote: Also, a countertrend trade in a strong trend needs a 5 minute (not a 3 or 1 minute) reversal bar.
candidates.description: A countertrend reversal-bar signal against a strong trend is only valid if the signal bar comes from at least a 5-minute chart; a reversal bar on a 1 or 3 minute chart is not sufficient.
candidates.pseudocode: // requires knowing/deciding the signal bar's own timeframe relative to the strategy's bar series - not expressible as a plain price/volume comparison without that design decision

complexity.reason: requires a design decision on how the engine represents/compares signal-bar timeframe when the strategy itself may run on a finer bar series (ties to Chapter 13's surrogate-timeframe candidates)

rejected.quote: When a stock has an earnings report after the close, some traders try to trade them because the big moves appear to offer great profit potential, but these moves are very difficult to scalp and most traders should not attempt it.
rejected.reason: requires knowledge of scheduled earnings-report timing, external calendar data the engine does not have

rejected.quote: It is not necessary to look at Globex prices when trading the day session since very little is gained... I prefer the day session chart, since trend lines and trend channel lines that extend over two or more days are very reliable on the day session charts
rejected.reason: a data-source/chart preference (which session's bars to load), not a bar-level trading condition

rejected.quote: A day session trader did not need to see the Globex expanding triangle to go short at bar 5.
rejected.reason: illustrates that day-session-only price action reproduces the same signal as the 24-hour Globex chart; not a new testable condition beyond patterns already mined elsewhere

chapter_summary: A short chapter arguing that price action works the same around the clock (Globex, premarket, postmarket, overnight), but that most of these sessions offer too few or too erratic entries for most traders, and that the day session alone gives adequate signals without needing to watch Globex. The two genuinely new, reusable ideas are treating the premarket/overnight extreme as a target commonly retested during the day session, and a pair of stated preconditions for countertrend trades against a strong trend: a prior trend-line break, and a reversal bar from at least a 5-minute chart. Figures 14.1-14.4 are worked examples reapplying already-mined patterns (high1, inside/outside bars, wedge, breakout pullback, double top, second entries) to premarket/postmarket/Globex charts and did not add further candidates.
